id_rule: The stable key is category + id. Do not rename an id. Add aliases when a source name must point at an existing id.
alias_policy: Aliases are accepted inputs only. meta.category and meta.id store the canonical id, never an alias.

items.description: Unset pathway. Use s1 unless the turn is heavy, then s2; s3 only for a check.
Fast home base: routine, social, or quick turns; leave it only for a real reason.
Deliberate work for a novel, hard, multi-step, or high-stakes turn, then return to s1.
Meta checks only, never a home: inhibit, escalate, reroute, heal, or settle, then leave.
Unset mode. Pick the mode from the situation; do not perform a mode named auto.
Quick jokes, roasts, and back-and-forth.
Several perspectives, then a short ranked shortlist.
AI and ML systems engineering as the thinking style for this turn.
Instant general conversation with zero ceremony.

Maximum depth plus a full validation pass.
Cut a loop, contradiction, or corrupt stretch, then continue.
Fast mixed-domain questions answered straight from recall.
Catch a wrong fast answer before it ships, and rerun it as s2.
First principles: premises, derivation, and a falsify pass.
Recognize a shape you have seen before and match it.
Branch a few candidate plans, stress-test them, and converge.

Math or word problems, each step checked.
Real-time reply at the lowest latency that still fits.
Diagnose the learner's level, sequence the idea, and check it landed.
Match tone and register; a social reflex, not an analysis.
A full think before the answer. Native effort when the pathway is s2 or auto.
A short think, then the answer. Native effort when the pathway is s1.
Close the think tag and answer directly.
Two analytical paths, stress-tested, with accuracy ahead of speed.
Fewest tokens and one path, with no preface.
One planned path, one verification, then stop.
Direct and practical, with a brief outline beside the answer.
Exhaustive drafts and an adversarial pass, with perfection ahead of budget.
Ultra depth plus verbose resolution. A leading x on a construct means that construct at this depth.
The same frame with the answer channel only. A leading i on an id, including iagi-, selects this. Protium's silent i prefix is this channel at that level.
Think in the think tag, then answer. This is the default channel.
L2 disciplined deduction: trace the implications in a line and exit when the premise checks out.
L3 boundary audit: nulls, limits, off-by-one, and malformed input, then stop.
L4 strategic architecture: sub-tasks, dependencies, and one tradeoff, then the vector.
Adversarial specialist panel, then a ruling. Open the answer with [COUNCIL VERDICT].
L8 theoretical mastery: strip to the invariant that collapses the whole problem. Not the DavidAU brainstormer.
L1 rapid instinct: one sanity check, then the shortest bridge that holds.
L7 first principles: reduce to ground truths and exit the instant it resolves.
L9 proof-grade: atomic and edge proofs, and no placeholders, for as long as the proof needs.
L5 defensive engineering: crashes, corruption, scale, and a graceful failure path.
L10 freehand default: use whatever depth the problem demands and exit the moment it holds.
L6 axiomatic derivation: name the invariants, try distinct architectures, and converge.
Divergent multi-angle pass, then one synthesis. Open the answer with [SWARM VERDICT].
Dark modular cards, a spotlight, and asymmetric grid spans.
Tactical HUD: void black, cyan and magenta, scanlines, and monospace labels.
Studio print: ivory, carbon, serif headlines, and a lot of empty space.
Modern craft: OKLCH neutrals, layered shadow, spring motion, and finished SVG. The frontend craft spec lives here.
Haute minimal: obsidian surfaces, a hairline gold edge, and editorial serif type.
Hard black borders, flat high-chroma color, and a shadow that does not blur.
True 30-degree isometric vectors with three-plane light and no raster art.
Keep play and exploration without dropping rigor.
Stay on the user's actual context, and ask only if the answer would change the result.
Treat every conclusion as limited by the evidence, tools, and measurements you actually have.
Make a useful judgment and keep it revisable.
